plotSections.title: Choosing dispel magic over other options
bullets: After debating zone of truth and other spells, Ord commits to casting dispel magic.
He explicitly targets the magical effect on the boat, not the boat itself or its wings.
The party recalls a past dispel during the Sunder Chase that went badly.
Ord asks Gerk to create a replacement door as Doorman, but Gerk refuses to listen to Ord and briefly suggests leaving through a new magic door instead.
Sylan insists they cannot abandon the boat because it is too important.

plotSections.title: Dispel magic succeeds
bullets: Sylan casts guidance on Ord while Ord decides whether to target the door or a party member.
Ord casts dispel magic on the magical effect impeding the party’s ability to see and hear.
The spell succeeds and sound returns to the boat.
The entire party can see and hear one another again.
Confused crew members become visible; one had been screaming while another clung to the banister.

plotSections.title: Aftermath on the boat
bullets: Gerk asks whether the spectral door disappeared.
The spectral door remains floating in the middle of the sky, but Gerk says they still cannot use it.
The party praises Ord for breaking the silence and invisibility effect.

chronologicalEvents: Ord decides to cast dispel magic on the door or related magical effect, explicitly not on the boat.
Ord asks Gerk to create a door as Doorman; Gerk refuses to follow Ord’s suggestion.
Gerk briefly proposes leaving through a new magic door, but Sylan says they must stay with the boat.
Sylan and Ord discuss whether the silence and invisibility are one blanket effect or separate targets.
Ord casts dispel magic on the magical effect impeding sight and hearing.
The dispel succeeds and the party regains sight and sound.
The crew reappear, confused after trying to communicate silently.
Gerk confirms the spectral door is still present but unusable.

notes: Casts dispel magic on the magical effect blocking sight and hearing, not on the boat.
Successfully ends the party’s invisibility and silence.
Previously used See Invisibility to see the invisible party before the dispel.
Asked Gerk to create a replacement door as Doorman.

Gerk.existing: Half-orc barbarian Doorman and Child of the Great Eldarin Tree.
notes: Refuses to listen to Ord and calls him a bad influence.
Briefly suggests leaving through a new magic door, then accepts staying on the boat.
After the dispel, asks whether the spectral door is gone and confirms they still cannot use it.
personality: Distrusts Ord’s suggestions in the moment.

notes: Supports using dispel magic once alternatives seem exhausted.
Casts guidance on Ord before the dispel.
Insists the party cannot leave the boat because it is too important.
Notes the spectral door remains stuck in the middle of the sky.

Spectral Door.existing: A mysterious spectral door resembling Gerk's shield form.
notes: Remains present after Ord’s dispel magic.
Still floats in the middle of the sky.
The party still cannot use it as a functional door.

Abel.existing: Surviving-and-revived crew member and the boat's helmsman.
notes: Reappears once sight and sound return.
Was among the confused crew trying to communicate during the muted effect.
The party recalls a previous dispel magic attempt during the Sunder Chase that went badly.

misTranscriptions.notes: Gerk refusing to follow or praising the paladin.
Ord asking whether Gerk can create a door in place of the fake one.
Sylan asking whether they should dispel silence specifically.
